```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_data <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE) &&
  nzchar(system.file("extdata", "spatial_aggregation.rds", package = "varunayan"))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = has_data,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, fig.dpi = 150,
  warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, out.width = "100%"
)
```

ERA5 and IMD give data on regular grids. When we aggregate a grid to districts, a small district can contain no grid point. Then that district has no value.

This article compares two methods of `aggregate_to_polygons()`:

- Point-in-polygon (`point_in_polygon`): the mean of all grid points inside each district.
- Nearest centroid (`nearest_centroid`): the value of the grid point nearest to a point inside each district.

```{r libraries}
library(varunayan)
```

## District boundaries and climate data

`load_india_boundaries("district")` gives the LGD district boundaries from [geo.bharatviz.org](https://geo.bharatviz.org). The function downloads the file one time and keeps it in a cache.

```{r boundaries}
districts <- load_india_boundaries("district")
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(districts))
```

We use two datasets for January 2023. The IMD 1° grid gives the mean daily maximum temperature (column `temperature`, °C). The ERA5 0.25° grid gives the mean 2 m temperature (column `value`, °C). The ERA5 download needs a CDS API key (see the quickstart). This article uses a cached copy of the two datasets.

```{r download, eval = FALSE}
imd <- imd_temperature_bbox(
  "india_tmax_2023", 2023, 2023,
  north = 37.5, south = 7.5, east = 97.5, west = 67.5,
  var_type = "tmax", frequency = "monthly"
)
imd <- imd[imd$date == as.Date("2023-01-01"), ]

era5 <- era5ify_geojson(
  request_id = "era5_india_t2m_jan2023",
  variables = "2m_temperature",
  start_date = "2023-01-01", end_date = "2023-01-31",
  json_file = "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/admin/India-geodata-lgd-states.geojson",
  frequency = "monthly", resolution = 0.25
)
era5 <- era5[era5$month == 1, ]
```

```{r load_data}
saved <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "spatial_aggregation.rds", package = "varunayan"))
imd <- saved$imd
era5 <- saved$era5
head(imd)
```

## Grid coverage

`compare_grids()` draws the grid points of each dataset on the district boundaries.

```{r grids}
compare_grids(
  ERA5 = era5, IMD = imd, colors = c(ERA5 = "#3498DB", IMD = "#E74C3C"),
  point_size = 0.6, polygons = districts, title = "ERA5 and IMD grid points"
)
```

`check_grid_coverage()` counts the grid points inside each district.

```{r coverage}
check_grid_coverage(imd, districts, c("state_name", "district_name"))$summary
check_grid_coverage(era5, districts, c("state_name", "district_name"))$summary
```

## Aggregate IMD to districts with the two methods

```{r aggregate}
pip <- aggregate_to_polygons(imd, districts, c(pip = "temperature"),
  method = "point_in_polygon",
  polygon_id_cols = c("state_name", "district_name")
)
nearest <- aggregate_to_polygons(imd, districts, c(nearest = "temperature"),
  method = "nearest_centroid",
  polygon_id_cols = c("state_name", "district_name")
)
both <- merge(districts, merge(pip, nearest))
colSums(!is.na(sf::st_drop_geometry(both)[c("pip", "nearest")]))
```

## Compare the maps

Gray districts have no value.

```{r maps, fig.height = 5}
plot_map(both, c("pip", "nearest"),
  cmap = "plasma", legend_title = "°C",
  title = "IMD Tmax, January 2023"
)
```

## Compare the values

For districts with a value from both methods, the scatter plot shows the agreement.

```{r scatter, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 5}
plot_scatter(sf::st_drop_geometry(both), "pip", "nearest",
  title = "Point-in-polygon vs nearest centroid (°C)"
)
```

## Conclusion

The 1° IMD grid is much coarser than the 0.25° ERA5 grid. Only 250 of the 783 districts (32 %) contain an IMD grid point. ERA5 grid points are in 751 districts (96 %).

With the point-in-polygon method, 533 districts have no IMD value. The nearest-centroid method gives a value to all 783 districts. Where both methods give a value, they agree closely, because most of these districts contain only one IMD grid point. With `fill_empty = TRUE`, the point-in-polygon method uses the nearest grid point for a district that has no grid point.
